subject: general
question: Which project aims to develop state roads along coastal border areas, including connectivity of non-major ports?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatmala.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharatmala **is a **centrally sponsored** and funded **road and highways project** aimed at improving connectivity across India.
 
• Bharatmala aims to develop state roads along **coastal border areas,** including connectivity of non-major ports, to promote** trade and commerce.**
 
• Bharatmala will greatly improve the **nation's highway system:**
 
 
• Increase the number of 6 NC **corridors **to 50 (n = 6 NC and 44 EC).
 
• Increase freight on **national highways** from 40% to 80%.
 
• Increase the number of districts from 300 to 550, all connected by at least **4-lane roadways.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The project is expected to cover a total of **83,677 km** of roads and highways and is estimated to cost around** Rs 5.35 lakh crore.**
 
• **Setubharatam Pariyojana** is a project aimed at **building bridges** in rural areas.
 
 
• ​An ambitious initiative called "Setu Bharatam" would invest** Rs. 50,000** crore to build bridges so that **traffic on national highways** can move safely and smoothly.
 
 
 
• **District Headquarters Connectivity Scheme** is focused on improving** road connectivity **in district headquarters.
 
• The **Golden Quadrilateral** is a completed project that connects **major cities** in India through a network of highways.
 
 
• ​It is shaped like a quadrilateral, with **Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai, and Chennai, **the country's four largest metropolises, serving as its vertices.
